correctness.rationale: On S² the squared half-chord is uniform on [0,1], so X=(1+log U)/2 has mgf exp(t/2)/(1+t/2). Forest edges are independent by leaf integration. Funk–Hecke and the Legendre equation give eigenvalues −1/[2ℓ(ℓ+1)] with multiplicity 2ℓ+1; absolute integrability and Hilbert–Schmidt trace give cycle cumulant τ_k=Tr(T^k), nonzero signed (−1)^k. For order below girth all multisupport cumulants vanish; at girth each shortest cycle appears g! times, giving c_g τ_g in the log MGF. Direct high precision zeta summation checks k=3..5, not the general theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The inner-product girth theorem uses finite-rank kernel eigenvalues yielding p^{1-g} >0, whereas the log-chord kernel has all negative harmonics and τ_g alternating with g, so that paper does not imply the evaluated zeta coefficients. The four-cycle work treats four edges, not all graph girths.
